title: ‘BusPatrol’ Put AI Cameras in Tens of Thousands of School Buses. Now They Want to Give Cops Access
summary: BusPatrol plans to scan the license plates of all vehicles the buses drive past, and then let law enforcement search that data. The plan would essentially turn school buses into roaming surveillance vehicles.
reason: This is a concrete example of enclosure in operation: commons infrastructure (public school buses, funded by public money and community trust) being converted into a privatized surveillance routing architecture that extracts data from public space and routes it to law enforcement.
angle: Use 'routing architecture' — the story isn't about what BusPatrol says it's doing (child safety), but what it actually routes: mass location data from public streets, through a private intermediary, to police, with schools as unwitting nodes in a surveillance network.

angle: Use routing architecture: data centers are not neutral infrastructure but physical nodes that route value extraction from distributed commons (energy, land, attention) into concentrated corporate hands, and local resistance is a routing-level intervention, not merely a representational one.
